This appeal having been heard and reserved for judgmen  coming on for pronouncement this day, Justice Hirdesh pronounc  the following:
 JUDGMENT Heard finally, with the consent of the parties.
2.

This appeal has been preferred under Section 54 read with Section 74 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act of 2013") against the impugned judgment and decree dated 19.10.2022, passed in MJC No.83/2020 by Reference Court.

sentences.text: 3. In brief, the facts of the case are that land acquisition proceedings were initiated by the Collector (Khargone), the appropriate Government under u/s.11(1) of the Act of 2013, by issuing the notification in this regard on 10.04.2015, stating that the State Government is of the opinion that it requires certain land at Gram Takli, Tehsil Sanawad, District Khargone ad-measuring 5.269 hectares for laying of railway tracks for the purposes of supply of coal to Khargone Vrahad Taap Vidyut Pariyojana (Mega Thermal Power Project).

In the aforesaid notification, various survey Ntpc Limited Through Maha Prabandhak vs Baliram on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109724678/
1 numbers were also given.

sentences.text: For this purpose, the General Manager (Project) of NTPC, Khargone was also appointed as the authorized Officer under Section 12 of the Act of 2013.

In the aforesaid proceedings, the Land Acquisition Officer/Collector has passed the proposed awards on 29.07.2016 and 30.07.2016, holding that the total compensation to the affected land owners would be Rs.1,17,20,829/-.

According to the appellant subsequent to that, separate tripartite agreement dated 16.08.2016, was also entered into between the land owners, Land Acquisition Officer and the NTPC agreeing to the aforesaid award and the additional amount as per the package.

However, the aforesaid award was referred to the Reference Court by the Collector, Khargone under Section 64 of the Act of 2013 on 28.06.2017, in which the impugned judgment and decree dated 19.10.2022 has been passed.

The Reference Court made the following issues after the reply was filed by the appellant:-
 Sr. Issue   No.
 1
Whether the award passed by the Land Acquisition   Officer/Collector is just and proper?

2 If yes, how much is the compensation of the As   acquired land? dated  the   the   
 3
Whether the reference is barred by limitation?
No  4 Relief and expenses?
As per  case  The aforesaid judgment dated 19.10.2022 is under challenge before this Court.

4. Ms. Surbhi Bahal, learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the impugned order is bad in law, inasmuch as the learned Judge of the Reference Court has not considered the fact that the reference itself was not only barred by limitation, but it was made after the landowners entered into a tripartite agreement with the appellant and the State, agreeing with the award of the LAO and also accepting the other benefits under the agreement.

It is also submitted that the learned Judge of the Reference Court has also erred in holding that the State Government was not the appropriate Government but the Central Government was and thus, has wrongly applied the factor of "2" in disbursing the compensation.

sentences.text:
Further, learned counsel for appellant has also submitted that the Reference Court has committed an error in interpreting the provisions of the Act of 2013, wherein, under Section 3(e), the appropriate Government has been defined, and admittedly, the land was acquired in the State of M.P., and the notification has been issued under Section 11(1) of the Act of 2013, which clearly provides that the notification has to be issued by the appropriate Government only, and a bare perusal of the notification dated 10.04.2015 makes it clear that the same has been issued by the Collector and the Officiating Additional Secretary (Revenue Department), State of M.P., Khargone,
in the name of the Governor of the State, for the purposes of establishing the thermal power generation units with its sites at Khargone, Nimarkhedi and Khandwa for development of dedicated railway track freight corridor for the appellant NTPC Ltd., who is responsible for building the aforesaid power generation unit.

6. Learned counsel has also drawn the attention of this Court to another notification dated 22.03.2016, again, under Section 11(1) of the Act of 2013, in which certain other lands were also included and one other land was excluded.
It is also submitted that the award was also accepted by the land owners, which is also apparent from the tripartite agreement dated 16.08.2016.

It is submitted that while passing the impugned award, the Reference Court has laid heavy emphasis on the fact that the land is being acquired for the purposes of construction of power generating unit,
which is being erected by the appellant, a Public Sector Undertaking, and thus, merely because the unit is being erected by the appellant, reliance has been wrongly placed on the notification issued by the Central Government on 09.02.2016, which provides that in case of rural areas, the factor by which the market value is to be multiplied shall be "2".

Learned Counsel submitted that the aforesaid notification would not be applicable in the facts and circumstances of the case when the appropriate Government itself is the State Government of M.P., and the power unit is also located in the State of M.P. only, and merely because the power generating unit is constructed by the NTPC, it would not make the acquisition proceedings to be initiated by the Central Government.
Thus, it is submitted that the impugned award be set aside.
7. On the other hand, Counsel for the respondent opposed the prayer of appellant and submitted that no case for interference is made out.

It is submitted that there is no delay in making the reference to the Reference Court which has rightly been decided by the learned Reference Court as it was well within the limitation provided for filing the reference under Section 64 of the Act of 2013,
which provides that the Collector may entertain an application within a period of further one year,
in addition to 6 weeks and 6 months respectively, as provided under sub-section (2) of Section 64 of the Act, and in the present case, the Reference Court has held that notice was issued under Section 37(2) of the Act of 2013 on 04.08.2016, which was served on the land owners on 16.08.2016,
whereas, the reference application was filed on 12.09.2016.

Thus, it is submitted that it is not a case where the reference was barred by limitation.
8.

In respect of the tripartite agreement, it is submitted by learned counsel for State that the same was made under coercion and is not binding on the landowners which has not even been referred to in the reply by the appellant before the Reference Court.

sentences.text: So far as the issue regarding the appropriate Government is concerned, it is the contention of the State that as per Section 3(e) of the Act of 2013, the notification is always issued by the Collector of the District only, and in the present case, for all the practical purposes, the acquisition was on behalf of the Central Government only, at the instance of the NTPC, which is a public sector undertaking and the learned Reference Court has rightly held that the NTPC being Government of India undertaking, and has applied the factor of "2" as per the notification dated 09.02.2016.
Thus, it is submitted that the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

10. Heard counsel for the parties at length.
11.

On perusal of record, this Court finds that the facts of the case are not disputed regarding the acquisition of the land vide the notification dated 10.04.2015, issued under Section 11(1) of the Act of 2013.
The first issue before this Court is, whether the award has been accepted by the landowners by executing the agreement with the NTPC.

Secondly, whether the reference was barred by limitation having preferred after the relevant period of limitation as provided under Section 64 of the Act of 2013, which provides that a reference has to be made by the person interested, who has not accepted the award through Collector, and the proviso to Sub-Section (2) also provides that the Collector may entertain an application after the expiry of the period within a further period of one year, in addition to, as provided under Sub-Clause (a) and (b) of Sub- Section (2), if he is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for not filing it within he period specified in the first proviso.
And, the third issue is whether the notification has been issued by State Govt. or the Central Govt. and who is the appropriate government in the present case.

12. On perusal of the record, it is found that the awards were passed by the Collector on 29.07.2016 and 30.07.2016 respectively in regard to land owners, whereas the reference by the collector was filed on 03.06.2017.

The learned Judge of the Reference Court has held that the notice under Section 37(2) of the Act of 2013 was issued on 04.08.2016, which was served on the landowners on 16.08.2016, whereas the reference was submitted by the landowners to the Collector on 12.09.2016,
and it has been held that the reference was within limitation.

It is found that if the landowners had filed the reference application on 12.09.2016, and it has been filed before the Reference Court by the Collector on 03.06.2017, which is well within the period of limitation, as the discretion lies with the Collector to entertain such application within a further period of one year.

Thus, if the reference application was submitted by the landowners to the Collector on 12.09.2016, and the same has been submitted by the Collector to the reference court on 03.06.2017, it cannot be said that the reference is barred by limitation.

13. So far as the contention of the appellant that the landowners had accepted the award by a tripartite agreement dated 16.08.2016 is concerned, this is not even pleaded by the appellant in their reply to reference application, although the aforesaid agreement is proved as Ex.D/1 in the deposition of DW/1 Mahesh Kumar, the Dy. General Manager of NTPC, which, in the considered opinion of this Court, has not been proved in accordance with law and despite the fact that it has been admitted in his cross examination by PW-1 Baliram, it cannot be accepted as a piece of evidence and thus, the contention is hereby rejected.

In such circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that merely because the NTPC is a Public Sector Undertaking owned by the Central Government, the land acquisition proceedings cannot be treated to be carried out in relation to the acquisition of land for the purposes of Union.
It is nobody's case that the acquisition proceedings are in respect of more than one State as provided under Sub-Clause (4) of Section 3(e) of the Act of 2013.

18. So far as the finding recorded by the Reference Court that since the land is acquired for NTPC,
which is a Public Sector Undertaking, the appropriate Government in the present case would be the Central Government, is concerned, , this Court finds that the notification was issued by the Collector in the name of the Governor of M.P. under Section 11(1) of the Act of 2013, and in the said notification itself, it is also provided that in column 5 of Schedule 1 appended with the aforesaid notification, the General Manager, NTPC, Khargone is also conferred the powers under Section 12 of the Act of 2013 as the officer to carry out the preliminary survey of land.

It is also stated that the proposed Vrahad Taap Vidyut Pariyojana is in the interest of public at large and has been given exemption from the provisions of Section 4 of Chapter 2 of the Act of 2013 which refers to the preparation of Social Impact Assessment study, and its publication is made separately.
In the other notification dated 22.03.2016, the same declaration is made by the State.
19. Thus, this Court has no hesitation to hold that the aforesaid notification has been issued under the name of, and by the authority of State Government only.

At this juncture, this Court can also fruitfully rely on the decision rendered by the Supreme Court in the case of Magnum Promoters (P)
Ltd. v. Union of India reported as (2015) 3 SCC 327 the relevant para 26 of the same reads as Ntpc Limited Through Maha Prabandhak vs Baliram on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109724678/

sentences.text: "29 . Further, on the plea taken by the learned counsel on behalf of Respondents 2 and 3 regarding contravention of Sections 3 and 4 of the 1972 Act for transfer of the land in question by the appellant during the pendency of the proceedings as it was acquired by NCT on behalf of the Central Government by placing reliance on Article 239-AA of the Constitution, with respect to the contention of the 1972 Act is concerned, the same has no application to the fact situation.

In view of the said provision, it has been contended by the learned counsel on behalf of Respondents 2, 3 and 4 that the Land and Home subject- matters that are in Delhi are still with the Central Government and therefore, the acquisition of land by NCT is the acquisition made by it on behalf of the Central Government.

This is a far-fetched argument of the learned counsel and therefore, the same cannot be accepted by us for the reason that the acquisition notification available in the original record would clearly show that the land is acquired by NCT, Delhi and not on behalf of the Central Government.
Hence, the said contention is liable to be rejected and accordingly rejected.
(Emphasis Supplied)

20. Although this decision has been impliedly overruled in the case of Indore Development Authority Vs. Mahohar Lal and Others reported as (2020) 8 SCC 129, but in para 365, it is overruled on the point of applicability of s.24 of the Act of 2013, and not on the point of appropriate Government.

21. So far as the decision rendered by the Division Bench of this Court in the case of Badrilal Dhakad S/o Late Shri Narsingh Dhakad and Others Vs. Union of India and Others passed in W.P.
No.16808/2019 dated 27.01.2022 is concerned, on which strong reliance is placed by the reference court, the same relates to the land acquisition for 12 lanes Delhi- Mumbai Expressway i.e., NH-148N under the National Highways Act, 1956 thus, admittedly, the acquisition was by the Central Government for the purposes of national highway, hence, the said decision is clearly distinguishable on facts, and has no application in the case on hand.

This Court is also of the opinion that when the notice is purely issued by the Officer of the State under the seal and authority of the State, treating itself to the appropriate Government, it cannot be interpreted to hold that it is issued by the Central Government and the reliance placed by the Reference Court on the notification dated 09.02.2016 cannot be countenanced in the eyes of law.
22.

Thus, in the facts and circumstance of the case, the finding recorded by the Reference Court that the appropriate Government in the present case would be the Central Government and the factor of 2' would be applicable, being contrary to law and facts, is liable to be and is hereby set aside.
Resultantly, the appeals are also allowed to the aforesaid extent.

No.16808/2019 dated 27.01.2022 is concerned, on which strong reliance is placed by the reference court, the same relates to the land acquisition for 12 lanes Delhi- Mumbai Expressway i.e., NH-148N under the National Highways Act, 1956 thus, admittedly, the acquisition was by the Central Government for the purposes of national highway, hence, the said decision is clearly distinguishable on facts, and has no application in the case on hand.
This Court is also of the opinion that when the notice is purely issued by the Officer of the State under the seal and authority of the State, treating itself to the appropriate Government, it cannot be interpreted to hold that it is issued by the Central Government and the reliance placed by the Reference Court on the notification dated 09.02.2016 cannot be countenanced in the eyes of law.
22.

Thus, it is submitted that the appeal is liable to be dismissed.
On perusal of record, this Court finds that the facts of the case are not disputed regarding the acquisition of the land vide the notification dated 10.04.2015, issued under Section 11(1) of the Act of 2013.
It is found that if the landowners had filed the reference application on 12.09.2016, and it has been filed before the Reference Court by the Collector on 03.06.2017, which is well within the period of limitation, as the discretion lies with the Collector to entertain such application within a further period of one year.
Thus, if the reference application was submitted by the landowners to the Collector on 12.09.2016, and the same has been submitted by the Collector to the reference court on 03.06.2017, it cannot be said that the reference is barred by limitation.
Thus, in the facts and circumstance of the case, the finding recorded by the Reference Court that the appropriate Government in the present case would be the Central Government and the factor of 2' would be applicable, being contrary to law and facts, is liable to be and is hereby set aside.
Resultantly, the appeals are also allowed to the aforesaid extent.
